title: Feature flag and experimentation platform (client)
summary: Remote flags and experiments that evaluate instantly at launch, stay stable during a session, can kill features in minutes, and produce trustworthy exposure data for A/B analysis.
requirements: Boolean flags, multivariate configs and experiments with targeting (country, app version, cohort, percentage).
Zero added launch latency; consistent values within a session; offline-safe defaults.
Accurate exposure logging only when a user actually sees the variant.
components: Config service returning evaluated flags for the user (server-side evaluation) or rules + seeds (client-side evaluation)
Local cache on disk; values snapshotted at session start
Typed flag accessors generated from a registry with owners and expiry dates
Exposure logger integrated with the analytics SDK
Debug menu to override flags in internal builds
tradeoffs: Server-side evaluation hides targeting rules and keeps logic central; client-side evaluation works offline and updates instantly but ships rules to the device.
Applying new values mid-session is fresher but can flip UI under the user; usually apply on next launch except kill switches.
Hashing userID + experiment salt gives stable bucketing without storing assignments.
body: **Launch:** read cached values synchronously (fast), fetch fresh in the background, apply next session. First-ever launch uses compiled-in defaults.
**Bucketing:** `bucket = hash(experimentSalt + userID) % 10000`; compare with allocation ranges. Logged-out users use a stable install ID; reconcile on login.
**Exposure:** log when the code path actually renders the variant, not when the flag is fetched, to avoid diluting results.
**Kill switch:** a high-priority flag checked on foreground; can disable a crashing feature without a release.
**Hygiene:** every flag has an owner and expiry; CI warns on expired flags; remove the code path after full rollout.
